budget_analysis.budgets: 25/50/75/100% of the total METHOD-book substeps of retrieval+rerun on the same request set; absolute substeps are always shown next to the percentages
budget_analysis.request_order: (task, init, request id), fixed before the run
rules: a request counts as qualified at budget B only if its joint pass is reached with cumulative cost <= B
failed requests and requests that end without a pass consume their full cost
an attempt that is still running when the budget ends is not counted as a success
budget_analysis.type: post-run relative-budget analysis (NOT a re-run with a stop rule)

analysis.full_trajectory_comparison: when recover and rerun (retrieval) produce the same candidate sequence for a request, compare the final execution arrays (actions, state, stage, per-object L/R forces, substep control index) and report every difference; nothing is tuned on the result
analysis.interpolation: every executed candidate is tagged direct_measured / interpolated / clamped_extrapolated from the library; interpolated candidates that fail are NOT called physically unreachable; prediction vs actual hold interval is tabulated by support type
analysis.interval: cluster bootstrap over the 8 (task x init) clusters, 10000 resamples, seed 20261101
analysis.median_ranking_sensitivity: offline only, from the same logs; candidates without an execution are reported as 'not executed'
analysis.never: no threshold, library, guard or policy change after seeing results; no write-back to the library
analysis.pair_vs_cluster: pair-level (32 requests/arm) and cluster-level (8 task x init clusters) results are reported side by side; cluster bootstrap over the 8 clusters only

arms.calibrated_lookup_arm: none (equivalent, see configs/calibrated_lookup_c1.json). Median-aggregation ranking is computed OFFLINE only and reported as sensitivity; its candidates may lack executions and are then reported as 'not executed'
arms.not_repeated: rule/rerun: development result exists (step12) and is not re-run on the new inits

phase_A_select_quality.selection: rule (face-value lower target, as in step12)

budget.cache: an episode reused from the in-process cache still counts as one execution of its attempt and is charged at its recorded cost in the METHOD book; the SPENT book is order-dependent and is never used per arm
definition: force candidate = one entry of the arm's ranking; at most 3 per request; the first execution of a request is inside the first candidate
guard retry = one geometry refusal by the execution guard that is followed by another try of the SAME force candidate with the refused grasp geometry excluded
3 counts retries and does NOT include the first try; the 4th refusal of one force candidate ends that candidate as guard_retry_budget_exhausted (no 5th try)

the count is cumulative inside one force candidate: recover arm = restores in one episode; rerun arm = whole-episode re-executions with the refusals carried forward (pre_rejected); both arms stop at the same 4th refusal
the count restarts for every force candidate (new episode, empty refusal list)
request-level bound 3 x (1 + 3) = 12 physical executions is DERIVED from the two rules above, not a separate allowance; it is audited per request (budget_audit.within_bounds)
one single function (run_request in s20_selection_eval.py) implements the loop for every arm; only the executor's on_refusal mode differs
budget.step12_relation: step12 (dev inits 26-29) used b1: recover = max 3 restores per episode (same as b2), rerun = refusals per force candidate uncapped with only the 12-execution request cap. The maximum refusals in any single force candidate in step12 was 2, so b1 and b2 give identical decisions on that data; step12 results are therefore not re-run, and rule+rerun from step12 is NOT stitched into this evaluation.

known_limits_to_state_with_results: library supports directly 2 of 8 pool candidates; others are interpolated between lo=1 and lo=35 anchors
same-task same-object reuse only; no cross-task transfer claim
guard and contact policy were tuned on T0/T7 inits 26-27, which are not in this evaluation
rule baseline is a face-value rule; the library is information-equivalent to a calibrated lookup, so a 'better than calibration' claim is not tested
no_preset_expectation: no direction of improvement is assumed; null and negative results are reported with the same tables
prerequisites_before_running: DONE: logging fields implemented in synthesis_v2/program_executor.py and verified not to change execution (reports/step20_behavior_probe)
DONE: full test suite passed before the freeze commit (see FREEZE_MANIFEST.tests)
primary_outcomes: first-candidate task + manner(force band) + contact joint pass, per selection
final joint pass within the fixed candidate budget b2 (3 force candidates; 3 guard retries per force candidate)
complete generation cost per request, failed requests included (METHOD book substeps; spent book reported separately and never used as per-arm cost)
same selection: rerun vs recover agreement of candidate sequence, per-candidate verdicts, hold_min/hold_max (retrieval arm only, phase B)

qualified requests within a fixed physical budget, computed offline from the logs: budgets = {0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1.0} x total METHOD substeps of retrieval_rerun; requests ordered by (task, init, request id)
questions: does measured-response retrieval beat the face-value rule on the first candidate and on final joint pass within the fixed candidate budget?
does stage recovery keep candidates/verdicts identical to whole-episode rerun and raise qualified output per fixed physical budget?

per_execution.parameter_effective_stage: force candidate -> first grasp instance of the requested role; geometry rejection -> approach instance
per_execution.substeps: executed_total, formal_rows, discarded_total_listed, discarded_by_guard_restore, discarded_planner_lookahead, executed_after_last_restore, prefix_rows_not_resimulated, identity_executed_eq_formal_plus_discarded

per_refusal (execution.guard_events[]).approach_instance: stage instance whose re-plan makes the exclusion effective
per_refusal (execution.guard_events[]).state_digest_snapshot/state_digest_after: sha256 identity of the restored state

scope.clusters: 8 (task x init); request-level pairs are NOT independent within an init
scope.init_basis: reports/archive_20261101/init_usage_ledger.json: T0/T7 inits 30-49 never used in any file under reports/; 22-25 were used for repair, 26-29 for the previous evaluation (and tuning on 26-27)

requests.text: hold the object with a very light grip
hold the object with a moderate grip
hold the object with a firm grip
hold the object with a very firm grip

shared_across_arms.episode_cache: per (task, init, candidate, guard-state); cache hits are charged at recorded cost in the METHOD book

pass_criterion.definition: task_ok AND measurement_valid AND grasp_stable AND hold_min >= band_lo AND hold_max <= band_hi, for the requested object only
pass_criterion.explicitly_not: this is a DEVELOPMENT criterion. It is not a qualified-demonstration yield: it contains no contact-policy verdict, no stage-speed check, no pair logic and no safety conclusion.
pass_criterion.judge: scripts/mt/s8_task_force.py per_object() (unchanged) on the executed episode
pass_criterion.name: task_and_force_band_checks_passed

status: FROZEN (budget definition v2); run only through scripts/mt/s20_selection_eval.py, which verifies reports/step20_selection_eval/FREEZE_MANIFEST.json
version_note: v2 supersedes the unrun v1 plan (commit 43e3c9b): budget wording replaced by the explicit definition below, recovery/candidate-source logging implemented, interpolation marked, wording of the retrieval-vs-calibration statement fixed.

boundaries: library supports directly only 2 of 8 pool candidates (lo=1 and lo=35 anchors); others are interpolated or clamped
same-task same-object reuse only; one stage window; 8 clusters
the rule baseline is the face-value rule, not a tuned heuristic
wording.retrieval_vs_calibration: same type of information, not algorithmically equivalent: full orders differ for 2 of 8 offline test cases, first choice differs for 1 of 8 (reports/step18_lookup_equivalence)
